model.mdp.stg_bars.name: stg_bars
model.mdp.stg_bars.raw_code:
-- Silver: Flink's event-time bars, deduplicated.
--
-- market.bars is a ReplacingMergeTree, so a re-delivered bar may exist twice
-- until a background merge collapses it. FINAL forces that at read time — the
-- grain below is relied on by the marts and by the uniqueness test.
select
    instrument_id,
    bar_interval,
    window_start,
    window_end,
    toDate(window_start) as trade_date,
    open,
    high,
    low,
    close,
    volume,
    vwap,
    trades
from {{ source('market', 'bars') }} final

model.mdp.fct_instrument_liquidity.name: fct_instrument_liquidity
model.mdp.fct_instrument_liquidity.description: Per-instrument, per-day trade activity, including late arrivals.
model.mdp.fct_instrument_liquidity.raw_code:
-- Gold: how tradeable each instrument actually was, per day.
--
-- Uses stg_ticks including late arrivals: this is a question about the market,
-- not about our windowing, so a trade that reached us late still happened.
select
    instrument_id,
    trade_date,
    count()                                   as trades,
    countIf(was_late)                         as late_trades,
    sum(size)                                 as volume,
    sum(notional)                             as notional,
    avg(size)                                 as avg_trade_size,
    quantile(0.5)(size)                       as median_trade_size,
    quantile(0.99)(size)                      as p99_trade_size,
    countIf(side = 'buy')                     as buy_trades,
    countIf(side = 'sell')                    as sell_trades,
    (countIf(side = 'buy') - countIf(side = 'sell'))
        / nullIf(count(), 0)                  as order_flow_imbalance
from {{ ref('stg_ticks') }}
group by instrument_id, trade_date

test.mdp.assert_bar_grain_is_unique.name: assert_bar_grain_is_unique
test.mdp.assert_bar_grain_is_unique.raw_code:
-- A bar is identified by (instrument, interval, window start). Two rows at
-- that grain means the dedup in stg_bars failed, or two Flink jobs were
-- writing the same topic — which is exactly what happened once during
-- development when a job was submitted twice.
select
    instrument_id,
    bar_interval,
    window_start,
    count() as n
from {{ ref('stg_bars') }}
group by instrument_id, bar_interval, window_start
having n > 1

test.mdp.assert_ohlc_is_internally_consi.name: assert_ohlc_is_internally_consistent
test.mdp.assert_ohlc_is_internally_consi.raw_code:
-- high must be the highest and low the lowest, and open/close must sit
-- between them. If windowing or the open/close ordering invariant breaks,
-- this is where it shows up.
select
    instrument_id,
    bar_interval,
    window_start,
    open, high, low, close
from {{ ref('stg_bars') }}
where high < low
   or open > high or open < low
   or close > high or close < low

test.mdp.assert_vwap_within_bar_range.name: assert_vwap_within_bar_range
test.mdp.assert_vwap_within_bar_range.raw_code:
-- A volume-weighted average price cannot fall outside the bar's own range.
-- A tiny tolerance absorbs float rounding; see ADR 0007 on price as double.
select
    instrument_id,
    bar_interval,
    window_start,
    low, vwap, high
from {{ ref('stg_bars') }}
where volume > 0
  and (vwap < low - 1e-6 or vwap > high + 1e-6)

model.mdp.fct_bars_daily.name: fct_bars_daily
model.mdp.fct_bars_daily.description: Daily OHLCV per instrument, rolled up from watermark-closed 1m bars.
model.mdp.fct_bars_daily.raw_code:
-- Gold: one row per instrument per day, rolled up from the 1m bars.
--
-- Built from bars rather than from ticks on purpose. The bars are already
-- watermark-closed, so this inherits that completeness instead of re-deciding
-- what "the end of the day" means.
with bars as (
    select *
    from {{ ref('stg_bars') }}
    where bar_interval = '1m'
)

-- Every column is qualified with `b.`: ClickHouse resolves a bare `volume`
-- against the output alias `volume`, decides `sum(volume)` is nested inside
-- another aggregate, and rejects the query.
select
    b.instrument_id                                    as instrument_id,
    b.trade_date                                       as trade_date,
    min(b.window_start)                                as first_bar_at,
    max(b.window_start)                                as last_bar_at,
    count()                                            as bars,
    sum(b.trades)                                      as trades,
    argMin(b.open, b.window_start)                     as open,
    max(b.high)                                        as high,
    min(b.low)                                         as low,
    argMax(b.close, b.window_start)                    as close,
    sum(b.volume)                                      as volume,
    sum(b.vwap * b.volume) / nullIf(sum(b.volume), 0)  as vwap,
    argMax(b.close, b.window_start)
        / nullIf(argMin(b.open, b.window_start), 0) - 1 as return_pct
from bars as b
group by b.instrument_id, b.trade_date

model.mdp.fct_pipeline_health.name: fct_pipeline_health
model.mdp.fct_pipeline_health.description: Daily operability summary: throughput, latency percentiles, late-arrival rate and decode failures.
model.mdp.fct_pipeline_health.raw_code:
-- Gold: the pipeline's own report card.
--
-- Most portfolio projects can tell you what the data says. Rather fewer can
-- tell you how late it was, how much of it missed its window, and how much
-- never parsed at all. That is this table.
with ticks as (
    select
        trade_date,
        count()                         as ticks,
        countIf(was_late)               as late_ticks,
        quantile(0.5)(latency_ms)       as p50_latency_ms,
        quantile(0.95)(latency_ms)      as p95_latency_ms,
        quantile(0.99)(latency_ms)      as p99_latency_ms,
        max(latency_ms)                 as max_latency_ms,
        uniqExact(instrument_id)        as instruments
    from {{ ref('stg_ticks') }}
    group by trade_date
),

bars as (
    select trade_date, count() as bars
    from {{ ref('stg_bars') }}
    where bar_interval = '1m'
    group by trade_date
),

decode_errors as (
    select toDate(occurred_at) as trade_date, count() as decode_errors
    from {{ source('market', 'ticks_errors') }}
    group by trade_date
)

select
    t.trade_date                                     as trade_date,
    t.instruments                                    as instruments,
    t.ticks                                          as ticks,
    coalesce(b.bars, 0)                              as bars,
    t.late_ticks                                     as late_ticks,
    t.late_ticks / nullIf(t.ticks, 0)                as late_rate,
    coalesce(e.decode_errors, 0)                     as decode_errors,
    t.p50_latency_ms                                 as p50_latency_ms,
    t.p95_latency_ms                                 as p95_latency_ms,
    t.p99_latency_ms                                 as p99_latency_ms,
    t.max_latency_ms                                 as max_latency_ms
from ticks as t
left join bars as b on t.trade_date = b.trade_date
left join decode_errors as e on t.trade_date = e.trade_date

model.mdp.stg_ticks.name: stg_ticks
model.mdp.stg_ticks.description: Trades, typed, with late arrivals flagged rather than dropped.
model.mdp.stg_ticks.raw_code:
-- Silver: trades, typed and with the late ones marked rather than removed.
--
-- A trade that missed its window is still a real trade. Dropping it here would
-- hide the cost of the watermark delay; keeping it unmarked would let it leak
-- into aggregates that Flink deliberately excluded. So it is kept and flagged,
-- and every downstream model chooses explicitly.
--
-- was_late is a tuple IN, not a LEFT JOIN. ClickHouse does not produce NULLs
-- for unmatched left-join rows unless join_use_nulls is set: it fills the
-- column's default, which for String is ''. So `l.sequence is not null` was
-- true for EVERY row and the first build of fct_pipeline_health reported a
-- late rate of exactly 1.0 across every day.
with ticks as (
    select * from {{ source('market', 'ticks') }}
)

select
    t.instrument_id,
    t.venue,
    t.event_time,
    t.ingest_time,
    toDate(t.event_time)                      as trade_date,
    t.price,
    t.size,
    t.price * t.size                          as notional,
    t.side,
    t.sequence,
    t.latency_us,
    t.latency_us / 1000.0                     as latency_ms,
    (t.instrument_id, t.sequence) in (
        select instrument_id, sequence
        from {{ source('market', 'ticks_late') }}
    )                                         as was_late
from ticks as t

macro.dbt_clickhouse.clickhouse__snapsho.macro_sql:
{% macro clickhouse__snapshot_staging_table_check_strategy(strategy, source_sql, target_relation) -%}

    with snapshot_time as (
        select {{ strategy.updated_at }} as ts  -- Single timestamp
    ),
        snapshot_query as (

        {{ source_sql }}

    ),

    snapshotted_data as (

        select *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key

        from {{ target_relation }}
        where dbt_valid_to is null

    ),

    insertions_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key,
            snapshot_time.ts as dbt_updated_at,
            snapshot_time.ts as dbt_valid_from,
            nullif(snapshot_time.ts, snapshot_time.ts) as dbt_valid_to,
            {{ strategy.scd_id }} as dbt_scd_id

        from snapshot_query, snapshot_time
    ),

    updates_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key,
            snapshot_time.ts as dbt_updated_at,
            snapshot_time.ts as dbt_valid_from,
            snapshot_time.ts as dbt_valid_to

        from snapshot_query, snapshot_time
    ),

    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes %}

    deletes_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key
        from snapshot_query
    ),
    {% endif %}

    insertions as (

        select
            'insert' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*

        from insertions_source_data as source_data
        left outer join snapshotted_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key is null
           or (
                snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key is not null
            and (
                {{ strategy.row_changed }}
            )
        )

    ),

    updates as (

        select
            'update' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*,
            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        from updates_source_data as source_data
        join snapshotted_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where (
            {{ strategy.row_changed }}
        )
    )

    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes -%}
    ,

    deletes as (

        select
            'delete' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_valid_from,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_updated_at,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_valid_to,
            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        from snapshotted_data
        left join deletes_source_data as source_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where source_data.dbt_unique_key is null
    )
    {%- endif %}

    select * EXCEPT (ts) from insertions
    union all
    select * EXCEPT (ts) from updates
    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes %}
    union all
    select * EXCEPT (ts) from deletes
    {%- endif %}

{%- endmacro %}

doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

---

### More information

- Read the [dbt viewpoint](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/viewpoint)
- [Installation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/installation)
- Join the [dbt Community](https://www.getdbt.com/community/) for questions and discussion
